Finding: Dashboard route cycles retain nodes and listeners
Evidence: Ten warmed dashboard checkpoints grew from 1506 to 3918 Nodes and from 5732 to 7871 JSEventListeners; Nodes rose exactly 268 per cycle and listeners rose about 238 per cycle; a separate four-cycle run reproduced the pattern
Likely impact: Long sessions may accumulate DOM and handlers and increase memory or duplicate work
Recommended action: Inspect unmount cleanup in dashboard and patient-registration ESMs and shared shell extensions; use heap snapshots only with de-identified QA data
Retest / acceptance criterion: After warm-up ten or more identical cycles should plateau near the same-route baseline

Finding: Forced-GC heap does not show simple all-cycle linear growth
Evidence: Heap was 26082044 bytes at dashboard cycle 1 and 25895244 at cycle 10; it dropped at cycle 3 then rose by 1790408 bytes from cycle 3 to 10; the test strict all-cycle heap-growth flag was false
Likely impact: A retained JS-object leak remains possible but the measurements alone do not prove it
Recommended action: Compare controlled heap snapshots and detached-node retainers after warm-up using non-sensitive QA fixtures; do not confuse browser JS heap with server Java memory
Retest / acceptance criterion: Retained object counts and forced-GC heap should stabilize across longer identical cycles

Finding: Dashboard starts a broad ESM payload
Evidence: The ten-cycle run captured 205 completed requests and 2821004 transferred bytes; 151 Script requests transferred 2466745 bytes or about 87.4 percent of the total
Likely impact: Download and parse work can slow first-use on low-bandwidth or low-memory clinic devices
Recommended action: Map initial chunks to visible extension slots and defer non-critical ESM activation; set a fixed-device transfer and route-ready budget
Retest / acceptance criterion: Reduce initial script requests and bytes without removing required dashboard content

Finding: Anonymous login downloads substantial assets before sign-in
Evidence: The ten-cycle capture recorded 55 requests and 1320093 transfer bytes including 35 scripts at 784907 bytes and 5 images at 246816 bytes
Likely impact: Adds transfer and processing work before authentication
Recommended action: Defer non-login ESMs and inspect the largest shared chunks and image assets under a fixed network profile
Retest / acceptance criterion: Lower uncached login bytes and requests while preserving sign-in behavior

Finding: Two shared scripts and global CSS dominate cold-route transfer
Evidence: The two scripts transferred 245975 and 221583 bytes on dashboard startup; the global CSS transferred 200860 bytes
Likely impact: Large common assets delay cold-route download and may increase parse or style work
Recommended action: Use bundle analysis and CSS coverage to find duplicate or route-ineligible code before changing chunk boundaries
Retest / acceptance criterion: Document contents and reduce agreed gzip budgets without a visual regression

Finding: Dashboard startup downloads workflow chunks beyond the home app
Evidence: Observed first-load chunks include express-workflow 108165 bytes; patient-registration 101590 and 89283 bytes; laboratory 82785 bytes; patient-search 65701 bytes
Likely impact: Hidden or route-only features may consume initial bandwidth and memory if activated eagerly
Recommended action: Map each ESM request to a visible dashboard slot and lazy-load only those not needed at startup
Retest / acceptance criterion: Every initial-route ESM has a documented visible or required reason to load

Finding: Republic logo is the largest login image
Evidence: The image transferred 171516 bytes and appears among the largest login resources
Likely impact: Adds avoidable bytes if the source image has unnecessary resolution or encoding
Recommended action: Check actual rendered dimensions and compare optimized WebP or PNG variants without degrading branding
Retest / acceptance criterion: Use an agreed image-size budget and preserve visual quality

Finding: Login still requests a missing badge
Evidence: The ten-cycle login network capture recorded HTTP 404 for badge_ksm.png
Likely impact: Wastes a request and can leave a missing visual or console noise
Recommended action: Deploy the referenced badge or remove or update the obsolete asset reference
Retest / acceptance criterion: No badge_ksm.png 404 on a fresh login load

Finding: Layout shift remains above a 0.1 target
Evidence: The ten-cycle unthrottled Chrome run measured login CLS 0.135 and dashboard CLS 0.168; dashboard LCP was 852 ms on this fast test setup
Likely impact: Visible movement can distract users and timings here are not representative of slower clinic devices
Recommended action: Reserve dimensions for images and async widgets; profile layout shifts under a representative device and network profile
Retest / acceptance criterion: CLS <= 0.1 on an agreed representative test profile

Finding: Login page requires 48 px vertical scrolling
Evidence: The separate anonymous UAT smoke run measured document heights 816 at 1366x768 and 768 at 1280x720 and 892 at 390x844; footer logos stayed visible
Likely impact: Adds unnecessary scrolling and differs from workbook TC002
Recommended action: Investigate the 48 px top offset and full-height background or container sizing without hiding login or footer branding
Retest / acceptance criterion: Document height fits each agreed viewport and bottom content remains visible

Evidence: The UAT network capture recorded HTTP 200 and 28636 transferred bytes for login-background_en.png
Likely impact: The previously oversized SVG transfer hotspot remains removed
Recommended action: Keep an image-size regression budget for the login background
Retest / acceptance criterion: The optimized background loads below the agreed byte budget

Finding: One authenticated audit attempt did not render the username field within 30 seconds
Evidence: The first UAT run stopped before entering credentials; a fresh public-browser check loaded the form and the next two authenticated audits completed
Likely impact: A transient bootstrap failure could interrupt sign-in but one occurrence is not enough to identify the cause
Recommended action: Repeat bounded anonymous cold loads and inspect failed requests or browser errors only if the timeout recurs
Retest / acceptance criterion: Repeated UAT cold login loads render the form within the agreed timeout

Finding: No dashboard request failures were captured
Evidence: All 205 completed dashboard requests in the ten-cycle run had no captured network failure
Likely impact: This tested route had no immediate failed-request symptom
Recommended action: Retain failed-critical-request checks in smoke tests
Retest / acceptance criterion: Repeated dashboard loads have zero failed critical requests
